Inventory-supported local pricing and a proposed LP exit
30 September 2026. Analytical refinement of the coordinated pDAI thesis. This study distinguishes
scenario assumptions, algebraic consequences and unverified integrations. It adds no chain observations
or transactions.
Proposed mechanism
Assume coordinated source issuance and accepted assertions, authorized Portal capacity, compatible
conversion markets and a system with more destination aT oken units than the corresponding pStable
units outside its control. The system repeatedly converts recognized inputs, buys pDAI, pUSDC and
pUSDT, retains inventory and offers inventory at a designated local dollar target. Dominant holdings and
control of important liquidity positions reduce the quantity of outside inventory that can oppose its
policy.
The proposed Ethereum exit is separate: ETH or BTC holders contribute actual ETH or WBTC to pools
paired with a compatible pDAI representation. Users trade against those reserves at variable rates. The
issuer need not promise direct one-dollar redemption. For analysis of that exit, a successful local peg can
be granted as an assumption. That assumption is not evidence establishing the local peg mechanism
itself.
What constitutes enough purchasing power
Let N be pDAI units outside system control that can become sellable during the supported horizon.
Include relevant unlocks, third-party mint rights and bridge arrivals. Let R be the target reference asset
and T the desired number of R units per pDAI. A zero-fee, fixed-price full-buyback commitment needs at
least N * T spendable R units. Real execution also needs fees, transfer availability and adequate timing.
For multiple stables, shared funding and competing claims must be consolidated once.
Let C(A, N) be the net R output executable from owned aT oken inventory A at the required scale, after
costs and competing commitments. Receipt-financed coverage requires C(A, N) plus other available R to
cover N * T and costs. The numerical inequality A > N establishes coverage only after a compatible,
adequately funded conversion supplies the required purchasing power. A quote for a small trade cannot
establish the conversion of billions of units.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 307

For example, 120 receipt units converted at an assumed net 0.5 R per receipt provide 60 R. They cannot
purchase 100 outside units at 1 R each. At an assumed net 1 R per receipt, the same receipt quantity
can cover that simplified buyback. These are specified conversion scenarios, not quotes for actual aDAI.
Underlying redemption additionally depends on reserve cash and applicable withdrawal checks; wrapper
sales depend on their own output reserves. Verified receipt and cap analysis (Appendix 49).
Repeated accepted issuance can renew purchasing inputs and avoid the need for new outside income at
each intervention. Portal outstanding exposure still consumes destination headroom until backing.
Income, purchases, existing holdings or valid mint authority over the exact underlying can fund backing.
The deferred campaign study (Appendix 34) records these separate balances and the examined cap
encoding.
Dominant ownership and two-sided support
If the system acquires all willing outside wallet holders through adequately funded offers, it can
determine its subsequent asking price. This is a strong inventory-control result. A posted sale at 1 R
constrains upward pricing when buyers can access it; a funded purchase at 1 R constrains downward
pricing when sellers can access it. Fees, transaction costs and route restrictions produce an executable
band around the target.
After inventory is sold back into circulation, holders can sell again. The policy must maintain coverage of
that outstanding inventory. With no outside trades, an ask remains a quote; successful purchases and
sales demonstrate execution. The system's token ownership and its share of LP entitlement must be
counted separately. Burned LP shares cannot be withdrawn by the system, and ownership of tokens
elsewhere does not confer ownership of pool reserves.
Under idealized assumptions of continuously accessible funded bid and ask, complete conversion
coverage, adequate target inventory and transaction execution, the support policy can enforce its
quoted band. The conditional proof concerns the funded policy and access, rather than token-unit
surplus alone. On-chain scheduling every ten seconds leaves an interval in which other trades can
change prices. A specification must identify which trade sizes receive support and whether support
occurs within the trade or later.
Standard V2 execution
For an ordinary fee-free constant-product pool, let x be its pDAI reserve and y its R reserve. A sale of q
pDAI receives:
R received = y * q / (x + q)
ending pDAI reserve = x + q
ending R reserve = x * y / (x + q)
ending marginal R/pDAI = x * y / (x + q)^2
With x = y = 1,000,000 and q = 1,000,000, the seller receives 500,000 R; the ending reserves are 2,000,000
pDAI and 500,000 R, implying a marginal ratio of 0.25. The pool began at 1 R per pDAI, yet neither this
seller's average execution nor the final spot price stays at 1. Fees reduce output. Subsequent
intervention can restore the ratio without changing the completed sale's proceeds. An external
willingness to trade at the target can attract corrective arbitrage, with depth and costs determining the
resulting band.
The actual Uniswap V2 pair checks that output is strictly smaller than the corresponding reserve and
enforces the fee-adjusted reserve product. An ordinary finite-input swap therefore cannot purchase its
complete output inventory. LP withdrawal is a different operation requiring the relevant LP ownership. V2
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 308

behavior is deterministic given reserves and input; the target-maintenance policy requires additional
execution and inventory. Pinned V2 pair, pricing and quote formulas. This algebra describes the standard
design, not a bytecode audit of every PulseChain pool or an assumed custom redemption contract.
Ethereum and BTC exit hypothesis
An LP provides a market exit by paying from contributed counterasset reserves. It need not create an
issuer redemption obligation or hold one dollar of collateral against each pDAI outstanding. Market
access nevertheless depends on actual available ETH or WBTC and changes as swaps alter the reserves.
Locking or burning LP shares can prevent the providers from withdrawing their proportional position. It
does not prevent traders from removing counterassets through valid swaps. In the fee-free model, if
pDAI input equals its starting pool reserve, a seller removes half the initial ETH reserve. Input equal to
nine times that pDAI reserve removes 90% of initial ETH. The remaining ETH is positive, but the quote
deteriorates. Locking shares establishes persistence of liquidity entitlement, rather than fixed exit
capacity or price.
ETH already committed to staking needs an actual liquidity or redemption route before it can fund an
ETH pool. A staking receipt paired with pDAI is a different asset pair. The Ethereum representation must
preserve legitimate transfer and bridge rights; WBTC also carries its own token and redemption
dependencies. None of these proposed integrations was deployed or verified in this study.
With interoperable pDAI and available arbitrage, the implied external price is:
USD per pDAI = ETH received per pDAI * USD per ETH
Ignoring fees and market impact, a pDAI fixed at 1 USD exchanges for 1/2,000 ETH when ETH is 2,000
USD and for 1/4,000 ETH when ETH is 4,000 USD. Its ETH ratio changes while its dollar value stays
constant. If an external pool implies another dollar value, connected traders have an incentive to buy on
the cheaper side and sell on the dearer side. Bridges, fees, limits and delays can sustain differences.
Fully connected markets cannot have arbitrarily independent prices while offering unrestricted
conversion. V2 market and arbitrage example.
Present conclusion and reproduction
The refined thesis is a managed local peg financed by accepted issuance, usable conversions and
concentrated inventory, with a separately proposed LP market exit. A funded two-sided policy can be
specified and proved under explicit coverage and execution assumptions. Receipt quantity and dominant
ownership alone do not prove the required execution. Universal external redemption is not required to
study that local policy; an independent dollar reference is required to distinguish dollar stability from
internal parity.
The explicit scenario manifest is Research/experiments/pulsechain_managed_peg_20260930.json; its independently
checked results are artifacts/pulsechain-managed-peg-20260930/scenario-checks.json. The formulas above use
rational arithmetic and exclude fees, external flows, borrowing, controller replenishment and actual
chain quotes. Scenario checks are illustrations of the stated predicates, not forecasts or an adversarial
simulation of the whole proposed system. No blockchain calls were made.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 309
